claim: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a serious therapy-limiting side effect of commonly used anticancer drugs.
source: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a serious therapy-limiting side effect of commonly used anticancer drugs.
evidence: This is a general statement about CIPN that is supported by established scientific knowledge in oncology.

claim: Previous studies suggest that lipids may play a role in CIPN.
source: Previous studies suggest that lipids may play a role in CIPN.
evidence: This claim references prior research findings, indicating citation-based support.

claim: High-resolution mass spectrometry lipidomics was applied to quantify d=255 different lipid mediators in the blood of n=31 patients drawn before and after paclitaxel therapy for breast cancer treatment.
source: High-resolution mass spectrometry lipidomics was applied to quantify d=255 different lipid mediators in the blood of n=31 patients drawn before and after paclitaxel therapy for breast cancer treatment.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology and sample size used in the study.

claim: Twenty-seven lipids were identified that carried relevant information to train machine learning algorithms to identify, in new cases, whether a blood sample was drawn before or after paclitaxel therapy with a median balanced accuracy of up to 90%.
source: Twenty-seven lipids were identified that carried relevant information to train machine learning algorithms to identify, in new cases, whether a blood sample was drawn before or after paclitaxel therapy with a median balanced accuracy of up to 90%.
evidence: This claim is supported by the machine learning analysis results presented in the study.

claim: Sphinganine-1-phosphate (SA1P) was found to induce calcium transients in sensory neurons via the transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) channel and sphingosine-1-phosphate receptors.
source: One of the top hits, sphinganine-1-phosphate (SA1P), was found to induce calcium transients in sensory neurons via the transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) channel and sphingosine-1-phosphate receptors.
evidence: This is supported by the calcium imaging experiments performed on primary sensory neurons.

claim: SA1P showed different blood concentrations between patients with and without neuropathy.
source: SA1P also showed different blood concentrations between patients with and without neuropathy.
evidence: This is supported by the statistical analysis comparing SA1P levels between patient groups.

claim: Paclitaxel inhibits mitosis by stabilizing microtubules and preventing tubulin depolymerization.
source: Originally isolated from the yew tree Taxus brevifolia, it inhibits mitosis by stabilizing microtubules and preventing tubulin depolymerization (Gornstein and Schwarz, 2014; Hershman et al., 2014; Yang and Horwitz, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy affects up to 80% of treated patients.
source: A serious dose- and therapy-limiting side effect, which it shares with other commonly used cytostatic drugs, is the chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy and neuropathic pain (CIPN), which affects up to 80% of treated patients (Pachman et al., 2011; Park et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous clinical studies.

claim: Currently, there are no pharmacologic treatments for CIPN except for duloxetine.
source: Currently, there are no pharmacologic treatments for CIPN expert for duloxetine (Pachman et al., 2011; Cavaletti and Marmiroli, 2020; Smith et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to clinical literature.

claim: Lipid mediators have been shown to be produced at high levels in sensory neurons, neuronal tissue and immune cells after chemotherapy due to oxidative stress.
source: More recently, lipid mediators have been shown to be produced at high levels in sensory neurons, neuronal tissue and immune cells after chemotherapy due to oxidative stress and have been shown to contribute to chemotherapy-induced neuropathy and neuropathic pain by modulating neuronal ion channels (Hohmann et al., 2017; Piomelli and Sasso, 2014; Sisignano et al., 2016; Stockstill et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Lipids are considered markers for neurological diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
source: In fact, lipids are already considered markers for other neurological diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS; Jensen et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2018; Igarashi et al., 2011; Kim et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The study was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki on Biomedical Research Involving Human Subjects.
source: The study was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki on Biomedical Research Involving Human Subjects and was approved by the Ethics Committee of the Medical Faculty of the Goethe-University, Frankfurt am Main, Germany (reference number 4/09).
evidence: This describes the ethical approval and compliance of the study.

claim: Sixty patients (one male, 59 females) with breast cancer and undergoing paclitaxel treatment were recruited.
source: Sixty patients (one male, 59 females) with breast cancer and undergoing paclitaxel treatment were recruited from the Tumor Center of the University Hospital Frankfurt, Germany (UCT).
evidence: This describes the patient cohort characteristics.

claim: Most patients (n=47) received the 'paclitaxel-weekly' schedule, consisting of 12 cycles of paclitaxel treatment (80 mg/m², each week).
source: Most patients (n=47) received the 'paclitaxel-weekly' schedule, consisting of 12 cycles of paclitaxel treatment (80 mg/m², each week); a few patients (n=13) received mixed carboplatin/paclitaxel treatment (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the treatment regimen used in the study.

claim: Of the 31 patients with a full set of samples, 17 had neuropathy after chemotherapy (54.9%).
source: Of the 31 patients with a full set of samples, 17 had neuropathy after chemotherapy (54.9%), 12 had grade 1, 3 had grade 2 and two patients with grade 3 (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the neuropathy incidence in the study cohort.

claim: A total of 255 lipids were quantified in each plasma sample.
source: A total of 255 lipids were quantified in each plasma sample.
evidence: This describes the scope of the lipidomics analysis.

claim: PCA yielded d=28 components with eigenvalues >1, which together explained 93.93% of the total variance in the lipid mediators.
source: PCA yielded d=28 components with eigenvalues >1, which together explained 93.93% of the total variance in the lipid mediators (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the PCA analysis results shown in the supplementary figure.

claim: On the emergent self-organizing map (ESOM), a clear separation of two clusters was observed, which provided support that the lipid mediators contained a data structure contingent with the prior classification into pre- and posttherapy samples.
source: On the emergent self-organizing map (ESOM, Figure 2a), a clear separation of two clusters was observed, which provided support that the lipid mediators contained a data structure contingent with the prior classification into pre- and posttherapy samples (Fisher's exact test: p=0.01054, odds ratio: 3.57 with 95% confidence interval 1.28–10.52; Figure 2b).
evidence: This is supported by the ESOM analysis and statistical testing shown in Figure 2.

claim: Based on the majority vote of the different approaches to feature selection, d=77 lipid mediators were found to provide relevant information on whether a sample was collected before or after paclitaxel therapy.
source: Based on the majority vote of the different approaches to feature selection including PCA importance and further univariate and multivariate feature selection methods, d=77 lipid mediators were found to provide relevant information on whether a sample was collected before or after paclitaxel therapy (Figure 3).
evidence: This is supported by the feature selection analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: With the top hits ('sparse' feature set), three different algorithms (logistic regression, random forests, support vector machines) could be trained to identify, in new cases, whether a blood sample was drawn before or after paclitaxel therapy with a median balanced accuracy of up to 90%.
source: In summary, with the top hits ('sparse' feature set), three different algorithms (logistic regression, random forests, support vector machines) could be trained to identify, in new cases, whether a blood sample was drawn before or after paclitaxel therapy with a median balanced accuracy of up to 90%.
evidence: This is supported by the machine learning validation results presented in Table 1.

claim: SA1P caused a direct calcium transient in approximately 11.7% of KCl-responsive sensory neurons.
source: We observed that SA1P caused a direct calcium transient in approximately 11.7% of KCl-responsive sensory neurons (Figure 5a and b).
evidence: This is supported by the calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: 73% of SA1P-responsive neurons also responded to capsaicin.
source: Stimulating SA1P-responsive neurons with capsaicin and AITC revealed that 73% of these neurons also responded to capsaicin and 25% of them responded to AITC, whereas only 9.6% responded to both stimuli.
evidence: This is supported by the calcium imaging experiments characterizing SA1P-responsive neurons.

claim: The second SA1P response was entirely abolished when the neurons were treated with AMG9810, but not with the vehicle.
source: The second SA1P response was entirely abolished when the neurons were treated with AMG9810, but not with the vehicle (Figure 6a–c).
evidence: This is supported by the TRPV1 antagonist experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: The response intensity to SA1P was similar between fingolimod- and vehicle-treated neurons, while the number of neurons responding to SA1P was significantly decreased after fingolimod treatment.
source: Comparing fingolimod- and vehicle-treated neurons, we observed that the response intensity to SA1P was similar (Figure 6g), while the number of neurons responding to SA1P was significantly decreased after fingolimod treatment (Figure 6h).
evidence: This is supported by the fingolimod experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Sphingolipids were significantly overrepresented among the top hits of lipids regulated between sampling days.
source: Specifically, sphingolipids were significantly overrepresented among the top hits of lipids regulated between sampling days (Fisher's exact test: p=0.01), that is while 46 of the original 255 lipid mediators were sphingolipids (18%) (Supplementary file 2), 11 of the 27 members of the final sparse marker set (40.7%) belonged to the group of sphingolipids.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the lipid class distribution in the feature set.

claim: S1P was elevated in the spinal cord of mice after bortezomib treatment and during bortezomib-induced neuropathic pain.
source: For example, S1P was elevated in the spinal cord of mice after bortezomib treatment and during bortezomib-induced neuropathic pain.
evidence: This claim references previous preclinical research findings.

claim: Blocking S1P1 receptor S1P1R with fingolimod effectively reduced bortezomib-induced mechanical hypersensitivity in vivo.
source: Blocking S1P1 receptor S1P1R with fingolimod effectively reduced bortezomib-induced mechanical hypersensitivity in vivo (Stockstill et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Targeting the S1P-S1P1R-axis was found to reduce paclitaxel-induced neuropathic pain in vivo in a preclinical study.
source: Interestingly, targeting the S1P-S1P1R-axis was also found to reduce paclitaxel-induced neuropathic pain in vivo in a preclinical study (Janes et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Sphinganine is a key branching point in the sphingolipid pathway, where it can either be acylated to form dihydroceramides or phosphorylated to SA1P by sphingosine kinases.
source: Sphinganine is a key branching point in the sphingolipid pathway, where it can either be acylated to form dihydroceramides or phosphorylated to SA1P by sphingosine kinases (Merrill, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research on sphingolipid metabolism.

claim: Accumulation of sphinganine has been previously associated with reduced activity of ceramide synthase CerS2.
source: Accumulation of sphinganine has been previously associated with reduced activity of ceramide synthase CerS2 (Pewzner-Jung et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Low CerS2 expression is a hallmark of various tumors.
source: Interestingly, low CerS2 expression is a hallmark of various tumors (Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The TRPV1 channel has previously been identified as an important mediator of neuropathic pain and is associated with exacerbated activity of sensory neurons during paclitaxel-induced neuropathic pain.
source: The TRPV1 channel has previously been identified as an important mediator of neuropathic pain and is associated with exacerbated activity of sensory neurons during paclitaxel-induced neuropathic pain (Jardín et al., 2017; Hara et al., 2013; Kamata et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: LPC 18:1 has previously been identified as an endogenous activator of TRPV1 and TRM8 and was found at elevated levels in murine DRGs 24 hr after oxaliplatin treatment.
source: LPC 18:1 has previously been identified as an endogenous activator of TRPV1 and TRM8 and was found at elevated levels in murine DRGs 24 hr after oxaliplatin treatment.
evidence: This claim references previous research findings.

claim: 9,10-EpOME was elevated in the DRGs of paclitaxel-treated mice.
source: Similarly, 9,10-EpOME was elevated in the DRGs of paclitaxel-treated mice.
evidence: This claim references previous research findings.

claim: Blocking 9,10-EpOME synthesis with the CYP2J2-inhibitor and the approved drug telmisartan was shown to reduce acute paclitaxel-induced mechanical hypersensitivity in vivo.
source: locking its synthesis with the CYP2J2-inhibitor and the approved drug telmisartan was shown to reduce acute paclitaxel-induced mechanical hypersensitivity in vivo and prevent paclitaxel-induced mechanical allodynia by pretreatment (Sisignano et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: LPA 18:1 was shown to bind to the C-terminal binding site of TRPV1 to increase the opening probability of the channel.
source: Lipid was shown to bind to the C-terminal binding site of TRPV1 to increase the opening probability of the channel (Nieto-Posadas et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The occurrence of neuropathy with the low dose paclitaxel therapeutic regimen is around 50–70%, and most patients (80–90%) are expected to experience Grade 1 neuropathy after 12 weeks.
source: Previous studies report an occurrence of neuropathy with this therapeutic regimen is around 50–70%, and most patients (80–90%) are expected to experience Grade 1 neuropathy after 12 weeks (Gornstein and Schwarz, 2014; Hershman et al., 2014; Yang and Horwitz, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous clinical studies.

claim: The cumulative threshold dose above which paclitaxel causes sensory neuropathy is 300 mg/m².
source: The cumulative threshold dose above which paclitaxel causes sensory neuropathy is 300 mg/m² (Park et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The algorithms trained on the analysis cohort data separated samples from the first from those from the second day in the second patient cohort at balanced accuracy of 0.6–0.62 and roc-auc of 0.65–0.69.
source: The classifiers trained at the analysis cohort separated samples from the first from those from the second day in the second patient cohort at balanced accuracy of 0.6–0-.62 and roc-auc of 0.65–0.69 (Table 3).
evidence: This is supported by the external validation results presented in Table 3.

claim: SA1P differed between samples 1 and 2 in the second patient cohort, which was consistent with its top ranking in the respective feature selection analysis.
source: After analysis, SA1P differed between samples 1 and 2, which was consistent with its top ranking in the respective feature selection analysis.
evidence: This is supported by the analysis of the second cohort data.

claim: LPC 24:0 did not induce any notable activation of sensory neurons at concentration of 1 and 10 µM.
source: However, LPC 24:0 did not induce any notable activation of sensory neurons at concentration of 1 and 10 µM (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The neuropathy lasted for several months or, in many cases, still persisted for 4.5 years after chemotherapy at the last examination.
source: The neuropathy lasted for several months or, in many cases, still persisted for 4.5 years after chemotherapy at the last examination (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the long-term follow-up data on neuropathy persistence.

claim: The separation of samples on the ESOM corresponded, but to a lesser extent, with the occurrence of neuropathy observed at the time of the 2nd blood sample.
source: The separation of samples on the ESOM also corresponded, but to a lesser extent, with the occurrence of neuropathy observed at the time of the 2nd blood sample (p=0.0328, odds ratio 0.16, 95% confidence interval 0.0137–1.022).
evidence: This is supported by the ESOM analysis and statistical testing.

claim: The small set of d=3 lipid mediators that emerged from all three univariate methods as top hits for neuropathy included sphingolipid sphinganine-1-phosphate (SA1P), sphingomyelin 33:1, and sphingomyelin 43:1.
source: The small set of d=3 lipid mediators that emerged from all three univariate methods as top hits for neuropathy included sphingolipid sphinganine-1-phosphate (SA1P), also known as dihydrosphingosine-1-phosphate (DH-S1P) sphingomyelin 33:1, and sphingomyelin 43:1.
evidence: This is supported by the univariate feature selection analysis for neuropathy.

claim: Statistical group comparisons verified that the three mediators differed significantly between samples from neuropathy-positive and neuropathy-negative patients.
source: Statistical group comparisons verified that the three mediators differed significantly between samples from neuropathy-positive and neuropathy-negative patients (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by the Kruskal-Wallis test results shown in Figure 4.

claim: A trend toward different SA1P concentrations in the plasma of patients after paclitaxel treatment was observed in the second cohort (p=0.086).
source: Furthermore, a trend toward different SA1P concentrations in the plasma of patients after paclitaxel treatment was observed (p=0.086, Figure 7).
evidence: This is supported by the statistical analysis of the second cohort shown in Figure 7.

claim: Paclitaxel was originally isolated from the yew tree Taxus brevifolia.
source: Originally isolated from the yew tree Taxus brevifolia, it inhibits mitosis by stabilizing microtubules and preventing tubulin depolymerization (Gornstein and Schwarz, 2014; Hershman et al., 2014; Yang and Horwitz, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about paclitaxel's origin, supported by citations.

claim: Paclitaxel is a standard adjuvant treatment for breast cancer and several other cancers.
source: Paclitaxel is a standard adjuvant treatment for breast cancer and several other cancers.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about paclitaxel's therapeutic use.

claim: Patients report a variety of primarily sensory symptoms, encompassing sensations like numbness, paresthesia, spontaneous pain, and heightened sensitivity to mechanical and/or cold stimuli in their hands and feet.
source: Patients report a variety of primarily sensory symptoms, encompassing sensations like numbness, paresthesia, spontaneous pain, and heightened sensitivity to mechanical and/or cold stimuli in their hands and feet.
evidence: This describes the clinical presentation of CIPN based on established knowledge.

claim: In more severe instances, the loss of vibration sense and joint position sense can further impact functionality in CIPN patients.
source: In more severe instances, the loss of vibration sense and joint position sense can further impact their functionality (Cavaletti and Marmiroli, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous clinical research.

claim: Chemotherapy can emerge post-treatment in a state termed 'coasting' where mild neuropathy can worsen, or new instances of CIPN may develop.
source: Chemotherapy can also emerge post-treatment in a state termed 'coasting' where mild neuropathy can worsen, or new instances of CIPN may develop (Flatters et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Several genes and neurofilament proteins have been implicated in paclitaxel-induced neuropathy.
source: Several genes and neurofilament proteins have been implicated in paclitaxel-induced neuropathy (Diaz et al., 2018; Sisignano et al., 2019; Huehnchen et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: A systematic approach to investigate lipids in patients with paclitaxel-induced neuropathy has not been performed prior to this study.
source: However, a systematic approach to investigate lipids in patients with paclitaxel-induced neuropathy has not been performed.
evidence: This identifies a gap in the literature that the current study addresses.

claim: Lipid groups measured included eicosanoids, endocannabinoids, oxidized linoleic acid metabolites, sphingolipids, lysophospholipids and free fatty acids.
source: Lipid groups measured included eicosanoids, endocannabinoids, oxidized linoleic acid metabolites, sphingolipids, lysophospholipids and free fatty acids, many of which have been previously associated with persistent pain states (Osthues and Sisignano, 2019; Shapiro et al., 2016; Sisignano et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the scope of the lipidomics analysis and references previous associations with pain.

claim: The biological relevance of the findings was validated in vitro by applying SA1P to primary sensory neurons using calcium imaging.
source: The biological relevance of the findings was then validated in vitro by applying SA1P to primary sensory neurons using calcium imaging.
evidence: This describes the experimental validation approach used in the study.

claim: All patients provided informed written consent.
source: Informed written consent was obtained from each of the participants.
evidence: This describes the ethical procedures followed in the study.

claim: Plasma was isolated from the blood samples immediately after blood collection to ensure lipid stability.
source: Plasma was isolated from the blood samples immediately after blood collection to ensure lipid stability.
evidence: This describes the sample processing methodology.

claim: Plasma was stored at –80 °C until analysis.
source: Plasma was stored at –80 °C until analysis.
evidence: This describes the sample storage conditions.

claim: From the resulting data, five patients had to be excluded due to incomplete lipidomics data (more than 20% of the analytes could not be detected).
source: From the resulting data, five patients had to be excluded due to incomplete lipidomics data (more than 20% of the analytes could not be detected).
evidence: This describes the data quality control and exclusion criteria.

claim: The remaining 62 samples from 31 patients were used for the machine learning analysis.
source: The remaining 62 samples from 31 patients were used for the machine learning analysis (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the final sample size used for analysis.

claim: The occurrence and severity of peripheral neuropathy was assessed according to the guidelines of the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) v5.0.
source: The occurrence and severity of peripheral neuropathy was assessed according to the guidelines of the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) v5.0, Published: November 27, 2017, by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
evidence: This describes the neuropathy assessment methodology.

claim: Neuropathy assessment was performed prospectively, before the first paclitaxel treatment and again after the 12th treatment cycle.
source: Neuropathy assessment was performed prospectively, that is before the first paclitaxel treatment and again after the 12th treatment cycle.
evidence: This describes the timing of neuropathy assessments.

claim: The last neuropathy assessment was performed 4.5 years after initial chemotherapy.
source: The last assessment was performed 4.5 years after initial chemotherapy (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the long-term follow-up period.

claim: In the present cohort, grades 1–3 neuropathy were detected following paclitaxel chemotherapy.
source: In the present cohort, grades 1–3 were detected following paclitaxel chemotherapy (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the range of neuropathy severity observed.

claim: Blood was collected from patients in EDTA tubes and immediately centrifuged at 2000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
source: Blood was collected from patients in EDTA tubes and immediately centrifuged at 2000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
evidence: This describes the blood collection and processing methodology.

claim: Approximately 2–3 ml of plasma was considered sufficient for each patient.
source: Approximately 2–3 ml of plasma was considered sufficient for each patient.
evidence: This describes the sample volume requirements.

claim: These lipids belong to the groups of eicosanoids, oxidized linoleic acid metabolites, endocannabinoids, lysophosphatidic acids, pterins, sphingolipids, ceramides, cholesterols, cholesterol esters, diacylglycerols, triacylglycerols, phospholipids, lysophospholipids, and free fatty acids.
source: These lipids belong to the groups of eicosanoids, oxidized linoleic acid metabolites, endocannabinoids, lysophosphatidic acids, pterins, sphingolipids, ceramides, cholesterols, cholesterol esters, diacylglycerols, triacylglycerols, phospholipids, lysophospholipids, and free fatty acids.
evidence: This describes the categories of lipids analyzed.

claim: Data preprocessing included examination of the distribution of the variables including evaluation of possible transformations along Tukey's ladder of powers.
source: Data preprocessing included examination of the distribution of the variables including evaluation of possible transformations along Tukey's ladder of powers (Tukey, 1977; Box and Cox, 1964), supported by visualizing the data using quantile-quantile plots and assessing the normal distribution using D'Agostino and Pearson tests (D'Agostino and Pearson, 1973; D'agostino, 1971) implemented in the 'SciPy' Python package.
evidence: This describes the data preprocessing methodology with citations to statistical methods.

claim: Data preprocessing suggested logarithmic transformation.
source: This suggested logarithmic transformation.
evidence: This is inferred from the data distribution analysis.

claim: Imputation of missing values was performed by means of random forests.
source: Imputation of missing values was performed by means of random forests (Ho, 1995; Breiman, 2001) implemented in our R library 'pguIMP' (https://cran.r-project.org/package=pguIMP Malkusch et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes the missing value imputation methodology.

claim: Only variables or cases with less than 20% missing values were retained.
source: Only variables or cases with less than 20% missing values were retained.
evidence: This describes the data quality threshold used.

claim: PCA focuses on the dispersion (variance) of the data, while clustering attempts to identify concentrations (neighborhoods) within the data, making PCA and clustering opposing methods.
source: However, among limitations of PCA is that it focuses on the dispersion (variance) of the data, while clustering/subgrouping attempts to identify concentrations (neighborhoods) within the data, making PCA and clustering opposing methods in this sense.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the limitations of PCA.

claim: PCA fails to separate data sets with non-linear relationships.
source: Furthermore, PCA fails to separate data sets with non-linear relationships, for which other projection methods have been developed, such as the currently popular t-distributed stochastic neighborhood embedding (t-SNE) (Van der Maaten and Hinton, 2008), which also has limitations and occasionally provides class structure to data sets that do not have class structure (Lötsch and Ultsch, 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge about PCA limitations, supported by citations.

claim: The ESOM network consisted of 4000 neurons arranged on a two-dimensional toroidal grid with 50 rows and 80 columns.
source: In the present implementation, the network consisted of 4000 neurons arranged on a two-dimensional toroidal grid with 50 rows and 80 columns (Ultsch and Lötsch, 2017; Ultsch, 2003).
evidence: This describes the ESOM architecture used in the analysis.

claim: For the supervised machine learning approach, a validation subsample of 20% of cases from each subgroup was reserved for final model validation.
source: For the supervised machine learning approach, a validation subsample of 20% of cases from each subgroup was reserved for final model validation.
evidence: This describes the validation strategy used.

claim: The approach assumes that if a classifier can be trained to assign a patient to the correct class better than by guessing, then the features needed by the classifier contain relevant information about the addressed class structure.
source: The approach assumes that if a classifier can be trained to assign a patient to the correct class better than by guessing, then the features, that is the lipid mediators in the dataset needed by the classifier to accomplish this task, contain relevant information about the addressed class structure.
evidence: This describes the rationale for the feature selection approach.

claim: In this use of feature selection, creating a powerful classifier is not the final goal, but feature selection takes precedence over classifier performance.
source: In this use of feature selection, creating a powerful classifier is not the final goal, but feature selection takes precedence over classifier performance.
evidence: This clarifies the primary objective of the machine learning approach.

claim: All tests were two-sided, without a directed hypothesis.
source: All tests were two-sided, that is without a directed hypothesis, without specific expectations as to which of the d=255 lipid markers would be regulated as an effect of paclitaxel and/or as a sign of neuropathy, and in which direction this regulation might occur.
evidence: This describes the statistical testing approach used.

claim: The tuning of the algorithms led to the selection of LASSO and Ridge regression as regularization methods for SVM and logistic regression, respectively.
source: The tuning of the algorithms led to the selection of LASSO and Ridge regression as regularization methods for SVM and logistic regression, respectively.
evidence: This describes the hyperparameter tuning results.

claim: The n=31 samples from day 2 were probably too small to detect whether a sample was from a patient with neuropathy using multivariate feature selection.
source: The n=31 samples from day 2 were probably too small to detect whether a sample was from a patient with neuropathy.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of the sample size.

claim: Although the three algorithms detected neuropathy in new cases at balanced accuracy of up to 0.75, the 95% CI of the performance measures was not separated from guess level.
source: Although the three algorithms detected neuropathy in new cases, unseen during training, at balanced accuracy of up to 0.75, while only the guess level of 0.5 was achieved when using permuted data for training, the 95% CI of the performance measures was not separated from guess level.
evidence: This describes the limitations of the neuropathy classification results.

claim: Univariate methods (Cohen's d, FPR, FWE) were preferred for neuropathy analysis, as well as a direct hypothesis transfer of the top hits from the day1/2 assessments.
source: Therefore, univariate methods (Cohen's d, FPR, FWE) were preferred, as well as a direct hypothesis transfer of the top hits from the above-mentioned day1/2 assessments to neuropathy.
evidence: This describes the alternative analytical approach used for neuropathy.

claim: Alpha correction for multiple testing was applied as suggested by Bonferroni.
source: Alpha correction for multiple testing was applied as suggested by Bonferroni, 1936.
evidence: This describes the multiple testing correction method used.

claim: The algorithms trained on the analysis cohort data were applied to data from the independent second cohort without further modification or training.
source: The algorithms trained on the analysis cohort data were then applied to data from the independent second cohort without further modification or training.
evidence: This describes the external validation approach.

claim: After excluding variables or cases with >20% missing values and imputing the remaining missing values, analyzed data of cohort 2 consisted of a matrix of size 52×239.
source: Specifically, after excluding variables or cases with >20% missing values and imputing the remaining missing values as described for cohort 1, analyzed data of cohort consisted of a matrix of size 52×239 (52 instances/samples and 239 different lipid mediators).
evidence: This describes the data structure of the validation cohort.

claim: Using permuted data for training resulted in algorithms incapable to separate sample 1 from sample 2 better than by guessing in the second cohort.
source: Using permuted data for training resulted in algorithms incapable to separate sample 1 from sample 2 better than by guessing.
evidence: This demonstrates that the classification performance was not due to overfitting.

claim: From the second patient cohort, six patients were excluded from the analysis due to more than 20% incomplete lipidomics data.
source: From the second patient cohort, six patients were excluded from the analysis due to more than 20% incomplete lipidomics data.
evidence: This describes the data quality control for the second cohort.

claim: Primary sensory neurons were cultured as described previously.
source: Primary sensory neurons were cultured as described previously (Sisignano et al., 2012).
evidence: This references the cell culture methodology with a citation.

claim: For calcium imaging experiments, neurons were stained with Fura-2-AM for at least 60 min at 37 °C.
source: For calcium imaging experiments, neurons were stained with Fura-2-AM (Thermo Fisher) for at least 60 min at 37 °C and washed afterwards twice with Ringer's solution consisting of 145 mM NaCl, 1.25 mM CaCl2 ×2H2 O, 1 mM MgCl2 x6 H2O, 5 mM KCl, 10 mM D-glucose, and 10 mM HEPES adjusted to a pH of 7.3.
evidence: This describes the calcium imaging methodology.

claim: Sensory neurons were incubated with SA1P or LPC 24:0 for 1 min at a concentration of 1 or 10 µM, respectively.
source: To investigate the effect of SA1P or LPC 24:0 on different TRP channels, sensory neurons were incubated with the lipids for 1 min at a concentration of 1 or 10 µM, respectively.
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions for lipid stimulation.

claim: The gold standard agonists for TRPV1 and TRPA1 were capsaicin (200 nM, 20 s) and AITC (allyl isothiocyanate, 75 µM, 30 s).
source: The gold standard agonists for TRPV1 and TRPA1 were capsaicin (200 nM, 20 s) and AITC (allyl isothiocyanate, 75 µM, 30 s).
evidence: This describes the positive control agonists used.

claim: Fingolimod was used at a concentration of 1 µM and pre-incubated for 1 hr prior to measurement.
